events.summary:
At 1229 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located over Denver, moving
southeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 45 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Hail may cause minor damage to
vegetation.

Locations impacted include...
Paintsville, Prestonsburg, Bradley, Oaklawn Estates, East Point,
Fitz, Lancer, Ivyton, Thelma, Dobson, Meally, Thealka, Collista, West
Van Lear, Dotson, Denver, Blue River, Buffalo, Swamp Branch, and
Hagerhill.

If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a sturdy building.

To report hazardous weather conditions, go to our website at
weather.gov/iln and submit your report via social media, when you can
do so safely.

events.region: Wasatch Plateau/Book Cliffs; Western Uinta Basin; Eastern Juab/Millard Counties; Central Mountains; Sanpete Valley; Sevier Valley; Castle Country; Southwest Utah; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Upper Sevier River Valleys; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Central
Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, Sanpete Valley, Sevier
Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book Cliffs, Western Uinta Basin, Bryce
Canyon Country, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper
Sevier River Valleys, Southwest Utah and Zion National Park. This
watch also includes recent burn scars such as Cottonwood, Widemouth
2, Forsyth, France Canyon, Monroe Canyon, and Black Canyon.

* WHEN...From 9 AM MDT Sunday through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Excessive rainfall is expected Sunday afternoon associated with
the arrival of deep tropical moisture across much of central and
southern Utah. Rates from 0.4-0.6 inches per hour are expected,
with isolated higher rates from 0.6-1.0 inches per hour possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
